extruderConfig.the_temperature_at_maximum_must_be: the temperature at maximum must be higher than the one at 0.

extruderConfig.the_c_coefficient_must_be_a: the C coefficient must be a number (for example 7.06e-8) or left empty.
extruderConfig.r_at_25_c_out_of: R at 25 °C out of the normal range (1000 to 10000000).
extruderConfig.beta_out_of_the_normal_range: Beta out of the normal range (1000 to 10000).

extruderConfig.the_connector_of_an_spi_sensor: the connector of an SPI sensor is the adapter board's CS, like spi.cs0 (or 1.spi.cs0 on an expansion board).
extruderConfig.this_sensor_type_is_not_edited: This sensor type is not edited here: it is kept as it is in modefff.g (only the connector and the name change).
extruderConfig.a_temperature_transmitter_that_gives_a: A temperature transmitter that gives a proportional voltage (0 to 3.3 V at the input). Enter which temperature matches 0 and the input maximum. Never feed more than 3.3 V into the board.
extruderConfig.pt100_with_the_max31865_adapter_board: PT100 with the MAX31865 adapter board (for example the Duet3D PT100 daughterboard) on the SPI connector. The connector is that board's CS (spi.csN). Wires: 2, 3 or 4 depending on your PT100 (the board must be set up the same way). Reference R: the adapter board's (400 on the Duet3D one).
extruderConfig.type_k_thermocouple_with_a_max31855: Type K thermocouple with a MAX31855 adapter board on the SPI connector. The connector is that board's CS (spi.csN). It has no other settings.
extruderConfig.thermocouple_k_j_t_with_the: Thermocouple (K, J, T...) with the MAX31856 adapter board (for example the Duet3D temperature daughterboard) on the SPI connector. The connector is that board's CS (spi.cs0 to spi.cs3 on the main board). Pick the thermocouple type and your country's mains frequency (50 or 60 Hz) to filter the noise. Mind the thermocouple polarity.
extruderConfig.two_wire_pt1000_straight_to_a: Two-wire PT1000 straight to a tempN input, no extra board. More accurate than a thermistor at high temperature; up to about 400 °C.
extruderConfig.common_thermistor_ntc_on_a_tempn: Common thermistor (NTC) on a tempN input. Beta and R at 25 °C come from the thermistor datasheet (the 100k one: 100000 and 4725 or 4092). Coef. C: only if the datasheet gives the Steinhart-Hart C coefficient; empty = 0. Up to about 280 °C.

extruderConfig.single_motor_board_it_has_no: Single-motor board: it has no heater outputs or thermistor inputs.

extruderConfig.heater_fault_turns_it_off_and: Heater fault: turns it off and warns
extruderConfig.solid_state_relay_ssr_for_ac: Solid state relay (SSR) for AC mains
extruderConfig.fix_what_is_marked_in_red: Fix what is marked in red to be able to save.

extruderConfig.green_free_orange_used_only_by: Green = free, orange = used only by another mode (Laser or CNC), grey = already used (hover or hold to see why). Tap a free one to put it in the new zone. config.g and the three mode files are checked.
extruderConfig.show_free_connectors_of_each_board: Show free connectors of each board
extruderConfig.output_and_sensor_the_board_connector: Output and sensor: the board connector where each wire goes. Pick it from the list (free ones first) or type it if your board is not listed (outN / tempN / spi.csN; ioN.out only with a relay; on an expansion board, "40.out0"). Beta and R at 25 °C: the thermistor's (the common 100k: R 100000 and Beta 4725 or 4092). Limit: the maximum the zone can never exceed; if it gets there, the board turns it off (M143).
extruderConfig.the_heater_is_controlled_with_a: The heater is controlled with a single sensor (the one above). Monitors are for safety: another sensor (for example a backup thermocouple or one on the housing) or the same one with another limit; if it is exceeded (or if the sensor fails), the board does what you choose. They do not heat or regulate anything. "Turn off all heaters and cut the power supply" only cuts the supply if the board controls it (M80/M81). "If below" also triggers with the zone cold.
extruderConfig.maximum_2_extra_monitors_per_heater: Maximum 2 extra monitors per heater (3 in total with the limit).
extruderConfig.danger_110_220_v_ac_mains: Danger: 110/220 V. AC mains wiring can kill or cause a fire: it must be done by someone who knows how, with the machine unplugged, with a fuse, wire of the right gauge and earth on every metal part. The board is never connected to AC mains: it only drives the relay input.

extruderConfig.each_zone_is_a_heater_with: Each zone is a heater with its sensor (and, if you want, monitoring sensors). You change the data here and

extruderConfig.zone_new_change: {zone}: new, {type}, heater on {output} and sensor ({sensor}) on {pin}, limit {max} °C

extruderConfig.err_no_free_sensor_number: {who}: there is no free sensor number; choose an existing sensor.
extruderConfig.explain_ssrdc: For a DC heater (12/24/48 V) that draws more than the board output can take. The board output only drives the control input of the SSR (the + and - of the output to the "3-32 V DC" input of the SSR); the SSR switches the + of the heater: + of the supply to the + load terminal of the SSR, the other load terminal to the heater and the heater to the - of the supply. Mind the polarity: reversed, the SSR stays always on or burns out. It must be a "DC-DC" SSR (AC ones, "DA", do not switch off on DC: the zone would keep heating out of control), with a heat sink and rated for more current than the heater. Slow PWM is written (Q10: 10 times per second) because the SSR takes a few milliseconds to switch on and off. Normal PID control: tune the PID of the zone.
extruderConfig.explain_ssr: The board output only drives the control input of the SSR (the + and - of the output to the "3-32 V DC" input of the SSR); the SSR switches the AC heater. It can go on a heater output, a fan output (outN) or an io (ioN.out). Slow PWM is written (Q10: 10 times per second) because an AC SSR only switches off when the wave crosses zero; with the normal frequency (250) it does not control well. Use a "zero crossing" SSR, with a heat sink and rated for more current than the heater. Normal PID control: tune the PID of the zone.
extruderConfig.explain_relay: A mechanical relay or contactor has contacts that wear with every switch: it cannot use PWM. On/off control is written (M307 B1 S1.0: on at 100 % below the requested temperature and off above it) and PWM of once per second (Q1) just in case. The board leaves no margin (hysteresis) in this mode: near the temperature it can switch on and off often, the temperature swings more than with PID and the relay wears out: plan on replacing it. Good for large, slow zones. The coil goes on an outN output (heater or fan) that gives the coil voltage; on an io (3.3 V) only with a logic-input relay module. Put a diode in parallel with the coil if the module does not have one. If you tune the PID of this zone, come back here to check it is still on/off.
extruderConfig.chg_to_on_off: switches to on/off control (M307 B1 S1.0), as a mechanical relay needs

extruderConfig.warn_io_relay: {pin} gives 3.3 V and little current: it cannot drive a relay coil; use a relay module with a logic input.
extruderConfig.warn_io_ssr: {pin} gives 3.3 V: check that your SSR switches on with 3 V (the "3-32 V DC" ones do).
extruderConfig.warn_spi_adapter: The SPI sensors ({pins}) need the adapter board (MAX31856, MAX31855 or MAX31865) connected to the SPI connector of the board; without it the zone gives a sensor error and does not heat.
extruderConfig.warn_m307_not_on_off: The M307 line of this zone is not on/off (B1 with S1.0): it is fixed on save.
extruderConfig.err_lines_missing: Lines of this zone are missing in modefff.g (M950, M308 or M143): edit it by hand.
extruderConfig.err_output_or_io_format: The output must look like out2 or an io like io3.out (or 40.out0 / 40.io1.out on an expansion board).
extruderConfig.err_output_used_elsewhere: {pin} is already used by something else in modefff.g or config.g (fan, bed...).

printing.while_it_lasts_the_red_bar_no_lights: While it lasts, the red bar at the top warns about it. To end it: Status > Lock cold extrusion, or restart the board. If there is a problem, the Emergency Stop.

printing.changing_or_reloading_fff_mode_does: Changing or reloading FFF mode does not lock it (modefff.g has no M302): lock it with the button.

printing.the_extruder_pushes_and_retracts_at: The extruder pushes and retracts at any temperature. The normal protection is off.
printing.there_are_no_heaters_configured_now: There are no heaters configured now (they are created when switching to FFF mode).
printing.the_extruder_pushes_even_with_the: The extruder pushes even with the nozzle cold: with cold material it can jam, grind the material or strain the motor. It is locked again when the board restarts or turns off.

printing.fff_mode_explain: In FFF mode the board loads what printing needs: the tool with its extruder, the nozzle and bed heaters, their sensors and fans, and the printing speed limits. In {mode} none of that exists, so the printing tabs are disabled.

pellet.reorder_title: Change the order of the zones
pellet.reorder_what: You are about to move “{name}” to position {pos}. The order would be:
pellet.reorder_nozzle: This changes the NOZZLE heater: it becomes {name}. The material temperature goes to that heater and the other zones are worked out from it.
pellet.reorder_i1: Nothing is heated or moved now: only the order is written into modefff.g (with a backup copy).
pellet.reorder_i2: The board uses it when you reload the FFF mode (button in the extruder configuration); until then the panel stays as it is.
pellet.reorder_i3: The steps are saved per heater and kept, but zone 1 (nozzle) has no step: if a heater with a step becomes the nozzle, that value is ignored.
pellet.reorder_i4: Afterwards check that each heater is still the zone you think before heating: a heater in the wrong place heats where it should not.
pellet.reorder_busy: A job is running: the order of the zones is not changed during a job.
pellet.reorder_err_no_h: The tool's M563 line has no heaters.
pellet.reorder_err_other_heaters: The heaters in the file are no longer the ones you see: reload the page.
pellet.reorder_err_no_m563: The tool's M563 line was not found in modefff.g.
pellet.reorder_saved: Order saved in modefff.g (backup: .bak-{stamp}). Reload the FFF mode in the extruder configuration so the board uses it.
pellet.feed_intro: Feeding only needs two things: a LEVEL SENSOR in the hopper (an input of the board) and a MECHANISM that moves the pellet (an output: the relay of a vacuum loader, a screw motor...). Without them feeding is manual: you fill the hopper.
pellet.feed_manual_note: You fill the hopper. If you define the sensor, the panel shows you when it runs empty.
pellet.feed_auto_note: When the sensor says the hopper is empty, the board feeds in runs until it is full or the maximum time passes (then it stops and warns).
pellet.feed_need_sensor: Automatic needs a level sensor: type the input (for example io3.in).
pellet.feed_need_mechanism: Automatic needs a feeding mechanism: type the output (for example out4).
pellet.feed_pending_reload: Defined, but the board does not have it yet: reload the FFF mode in the extruder configuration.
pellet.feed_save_note: Save writes the lines into modefff.g (with a backup) and, if automatic, the trigger macro. The board uses them when you reload the FFF mode. “Feed” tests the mechanism for those seconds.
pellet.feed_confirm_text: This is written into modefff.g: {lines}. Mode {mode}. If automatic, the board switches the mechanism on by itself when the sensor says the hopper is empty (in runs, with a time limit). Check that the sensor and the mechanism are wired to those pins and that nothing can jam or overflow.
pellet.feed_saved: Feeding saved (modefff.g backup: .bak-{stamp}). Reload the FFF mode in the extruder configuration so the board uses it.
pellet.feed_err_pin: “{pin}” is not a valid pin (examples: io3.in, out4).
pellet.feed_err_pin_use: Pin {pin} is already used by something else in the configuration: pick a free one.
pellet.feed_err_auto: Automatic feeding needs the sensor and the mechanism defined.
pellet.feed_err_trigger: There is no free trigger number in 0:/sys.
pellet.feed_pulsed: Mechanism on for {s} s and off.

pellet.coupled_pid_title: Tune the PID of the zones
pellet.coupled_pid_note: In a pellet barrel the zones are coupled to each other: tuning only one gives a false model. They are all tuned, one at a time and with the neighbours hot.
pellet.tune_pid_tip: Auto-tune of this heater (M303): goes to the PID tab with this zone picked

pellet.add_zone_hint: New zone added below, in the extruder configuration: pick the heater output and the sensor input (only free connectors are offered), check the data and save.
pellet.add_sensor_hint: Monitoring sensor added below, in the picked zone: an extra sensor that cuts if the temperature goes over a limit. Pick its input and save.
pellet.add_sensor_none: The extruder configuration has not read the zone yet: wait a moment and try again.
pellet.asst_intro: A screw pushes melted plastic, not a filament: if it starts at once it loses steps, and if it stops at once plastic keeps coming out. Here you set how softly it starts and stops (acceleration and jerk), the top speed and whether it can retract.
pellet.asst_preset_soft_note: Soft: the screw starts and stops slowly. The safest to begin with: it hardly loses steps, but the flow takes a moment to reach its value.
pellet.asst_preset_balanced_note: Balanced: a middle response, fine for most screws with a gearbox.
pellet.asst_preset_fast_note: Fast: the flow answers at once, but a motor without a gearbox or with hard material can lose steps. Use it only if the extrusion test comes out clean.
pellet.asst_preset_none: Your own values: they match no starting point. The starting points are a first guess, not a measurement; the extrusion test of the panel tells whether the motor holds them.
pellet.asst_accel_help: How fast the screw speed rises. Low: soft start, no lost steps, but the flow is slow to arrive. High: quick response, but the motor can skip steps or knock.
pellet.asst_jerk_help: The change of speed the motor takes at once, with no ramp. Low: starts and stops without jolts. High: quicker, but you hear a knock and it can lose steps.
pellet.asst_speed_help: The speed limit of the screw. If the motor clicks or stalls when it extrudes a lot, lower it.
pellet.asst_retract_help: Retracting turns the screw backwards to cut the thread of plastic. In a screw it is slow and not exact, because melted plastic compresses. Leave it at 0 (off) until you need it; if you use it, try 0.5 to 2 mm.
pellet.asst_retract_cold: It will not retract below {limit} °C and these zones are colder: {cold}.
pellet.asst_retract_g10: G-code with G10 and G11 uses it (firmware retraction); if your slicer puts its own retraction moves, this does not change them.
pellet.asst_test: Try it with the short extrusion
pellet.asst_note: It is applied now and saved in the manufacturing mode (modefff.g, with a .bak copy), so it stays after a restart. It is not applied while the machine is working.
pellet.asst_saved: Done: the motor uses these values now and they were saved in modefff.g.
pellet.asst_err: Check the value of "{field}": it is empty or out of range.
pellet.newfan_intro: You define the fan (name, output connector and frequency) and it is written into modefff.g with a backup copy. The board uses it when the FFF mode is reloaded.
pellet.newfan_part_note: It joins the tool: the job (M106) and this panel set it; it cools the part or the nozzle.
pellet.newfan_throat_note: It switches on by itself with the temperature of the heaters you pick: it cools the throat so the pellet does not soften too early.
pellet.newfan_note: The connector must be free (it is checked) and the fan wired there: without a tachometer the board cannot tell whether it turns.
pellet.newfan_confirm_text: The fan “{name}” on connector {pin} (M106 P{index}) will be written into modefff.g. Check that it is wired there and that the connector gives the fan's voltage.
pellet.newfan_saved: Fan “{name}” written into modefff.g (backup: .bak-{stamp}). Reload the FFF mode in the extruder configuration so the board uses it.
pellet.newfan_removed: Fan removed from modefff.g (backup: .bak-{stamp}). Reload the FFF mode so the board no longer has it.
pellet.newfan_log: Fan added to the pellet extruder: {name} (P{index})
pellet.newfan_err_index: There is no free fan number.
pellet.newfan_err_full: The board already has every fan number in use.
pellet.newfan_err_name: The name must be 1 to 24 characters, without quotes or semicolons.
pellet.newfan_err_pin: The connector is not valid (examples: out6, out7).
pellet.newfan_err_heaters: Pick at least one heater whose temperature the fan follows.
pellet.newfan_err_temps: The temperatures must be 0 to 300 °C and the full-speed one cannot be lower than the start one.
pellet.newfan_err_no_m563: The tool's M563 line was not found in modefff.g.
pellet.newfan_err_exists: That fan is already in the file: reload the page.
pellet.newfan_err_missing: That fan is no longer in the file (or this page did not add it).
pellet.setup_intro: This is where the pellet extruder is CONFIGURED: the heat zones and their order, the fans, the feeding and the motor. What you watch and run live is in “Pellet panel”.
pellet.zones_note: Zone 1 is the NOZZLE. Change the order with the arrows or by dragging a row: it tells you what that implies before writing. The step is how many °C colder each zone works than the nozzle.
pellet.connections_title: Connections, sensors and limits of each zone
pellet.no_fans: The board has no fans defined.
pellet.fans_note: This shows what the board has. Part fans join the tool; throat fans follow the temperature. Changing their speed is done in the “Pellet panel”.
pellet.motor_runtime_values: Now: flow {flow} %, pressure advance {pa} s (values of this session of the board).
pellet.motor_setup_note: Here the motor is only shown. Testing it, the flow and the pressure advance are set live in the “Pellet panel”; the steps per mm (M92) are calibrated by weight in “Extruder”.
pellet.layout_what: How the pellet panel (the one the operator sees) is drawn: with the extruder axis vertical or horizontal. It is a choice of the machine and it is saved.
pellet.step_readonly: Step of this zone: {c} °C relative to the nozzle. It is changed in “Pellet setup”.
pellet.advance_saved: Pressure advance saved in the configuration: it comes back at start.
pellet.advance_not_saved: Applied but could not be saved for the start: {error}

pid.tune_chart_title: Tuning of {name}: what the board measured
pid.tune_chart_help: This is how the model is calculated: the board switches the heater fully on and off around the target and measures how long it takes to rise, how far it overshoots and how long it takes to fall (here between {min} and {max} °C). The new model below (heating, cooling and dead time) comes from those swings. The service records it, so it looks the same from any screen and stays even if you close the page.
pid.tuning_of_all_zones_started_you: Tuning of all zones started. You can change pages; the system keeps it going by itself.
pid.understood_i_stay_next_to_the: Understood: I stay next to the machine
pid.to_stop_the_cancel_button_on: To stop: the Cancel button on this page (turns the zones off), or the Emergency Stop.
pid.the_barrel_and_the_nozzle_get: The barrel and the nozzle get very hot: do not touch them or leave anything on them. Do not load material or extrude.
pid.while_it_lasts_no_job_controls: While it lasts no job controls it: do not leave the machine alone.
pid.all_zones_heat_to_their_target: All zones heat to their target and are tuned one at a time: each zone heats and cools by itself. It can take 10 to 30 minutes per zone.
pid.zone_tuning_cancelled_the_zones_were: Zone tuning cancelled: the zones were turned off.
pid.tuning_of_all_zones_finished_check: Tuning of all zones finished: check the new lines and save them if you want to keep them.
pid.to_stop_status_turn_off_all: To stop: Status > Turn off all heaters, or the Emergency Stop.
pid.the_nozzle_and_the_bed_get: The nozzle and the bed get very hot: do not touch them or leave anything on them.
pid.the_heater_goes_up_and_down: The heater goes up and down in temperature by itself, several times, for several minutes (the bed, 10 to 20).
pid.tuning_finished_check_the_new_model: Tuning finished: check the new model and save it if you want to keep it.
pid.a_zone_is_in_fault_check: A zone is in fault: check it in Status.
pid.a_heater_is_already_being_tuned: A heater is already being tuned.
pid.the_machine_has_to_be_idle: The machine has to be idle.
pid.the_new_models_are_already_in: The new models are already in use until the mode changes. Save replaces the M307 line of each zone in modefff.g, all at once (with a .bak copy).
pid.to_stop_cancel_turns_the_zones: To stop: Cancel (turns the zones off), or the Emergency Stop.
pid.each_target_must_be_from_50: Each target must be from 50 °C up to less than its zone's limit.
pid.if_you_tune_a_zone_with: . If you tune a zone with its neighbours cold, it learns more heat loss than it will have when printing, and then it oscillates. That is why here each zone is tuned with the others already hot at their working temperature: first they all heat up, the zone being tuned turns off and waits to cool down (the board needs to start at least 20 °C below the target), it is tuned, and it moves on to the next one. It can take 10 to 30 minutes per zone. The system does it: you can close the page and come back.
pid.in_a_barrel_with_several_zones: In a barrel with several zones, the heat of one zone flows into the ones next to it: the zones are
pid.after_tuning_the_new_model_is: After tuning, the new model is in use until the mode changes. Save replaces that heater's M307 line in modefff.g (with a .bak copy).
pid.locked_heater_fault: {name} is in fault (reads {c} °C): check its temperature sensor and wiring. It cannot be tuned while it is in fault.
pid.locked_zones_running: A zones tuning is running: wait for it to finish.
pid.locked_temperature: The temperature must be between 31 and {max} °C.
pid.locked_machine_busy: The machine is not free: wait for what it is doing to finish.
pid.locked_machine_off: The machine is switched off: turn it on first (the heaters need the power supply).
pid.the_nozzle_and_the_bed_only: The nozzle and the bed only exist in FFF mode.
pid.intro: Tuning (M303) heats and cools several times to learn how the heater responds, so it can hold the temperature without oscillating. Do it with the material you use most and at its temperature, with the part cooling fan as you use it when printing. The nozzle takes about 5 minutes; the bed, 10 to 20.
pid.do_not_leave: Do not leave the machine alone while it heats.
pid.tuning_in_progress: Tuning {name}: {c} °C. You can change page; the result is read when you come back.
pid.phase_tuning: {zone}: tuning, the temperature goes up and down by itself.
pid.phase_waiting_cool: {zone}: waiting for it to drop to {c} °C or less and settle.
pid.wait_neighbours: the other zones to reach their temperature
pid.wait_zone_cool: this zone, turned off, to drop to {c} °C or less
pid.tuning_started: Tuning {name} at {c} °C. To stop it: turn the heater off (Status > Turn off nozzle and bed) or use the Emergency Stop.
pid.tune_all_zones_title: Tune the PID of all zones of T{n}
pid.could_not_cancel_use: Could not cancel: {error}. Use Status > Turn off all heaters or the Emergency Stop.
pid.saved_n_lines: Saved {n} M307 lines to modefff.g (copy: modefff.g.bak-{stamp}).
pid.lines_added: The ones of {list} were added, they were missing.

pidDetail.dead_time_very_long_for_how: Dead time very long for how fast it cools: it is close to the limit the board accepts (dead time × K up to 50).
pidDetail.little_power_margin_to_hold_this: Little power margin: to hold this temperature it uses almost all it has. With the fan or a draught it may not be enough.

commissioning.fff_mode_bltouch_offset_and_the: FFF mode BLTouch offset and the bed mesh: in Work zones (Offsets and Mesh).
commissioning.fff_mode_bltouch_offset_and_the_no_map: FFF mode BLTouch offset and the bed mesh.
commissioning.first_layer_z_height_and_mesh: First layer Z height and mesh

commissioning.it_is_marked_done_by_itself_3: It is marked done by itself when the bed PID is saved in the PID tab.
commissioning.same_as_the_nozzle_takes_longer: Same as the nozzle; takes longer.
commissioning.it_is_marked_done_by_itself_2: It is marked done by itself when the nozzle PID is saved in the PID tab.
commissioning.so_it_holds_the_temperature_without: So it holds the temperature without oscillating.
commissioning.it_is_marked_done_by_itself: It is marked done by itself when the flow is saved in the Extruder tab.

commissioning.with_the_nozzle_hot_purge_and: With the nozzle hot, purge and check that plastic comes out.
commissioning.the_part_cooling_fan_is_tested: The part-cooling fan is tested here; the automatic ones start by themselves when the nozzle heats up.
commissioning.at_rest_each_sensor_has_to: At rest each sensor has to read the room temperature (5 to 50 °C).
commissioning.if_the_screw_turns_backwards_nothing: If the screw turns backwards (nothing comes out or it pulls inward), change S of the extruder M569 in modefff.g.

commissioning.there_are_no_heaters_configured_they: There are no heaters configured (they are created when switching to FFF mode).
commissioning.commissioning_complete_the_machine_is_re: Commissioning complete: the machine is ready to print. If you change a head, a heater or a cable, repeat the steps that involve it.
commissioning.first_switch_the_machine_to_fff: First switch the machine to FFF mode (Head change tab).
commissioning.for_the_first_time_everything_is: For the first time everything is connected (or after changing a head, a heater or a cable). Do it in order: a badly read sensor makes everything else useless. What gets calibrated is recorded with the date.
commissioning.heater_test_help: Real test, one at a time: sets it to 60 °C (the bed and the chamber to 40) and checks that it rises {rise} °C in less than {min} minutes. Then it turns it off.
commissioning.went_into_fault: It went into fault: check the heater (wire or cartridge) and the sensor.
commissioning.rose_too_little: It rose only {c} °C in {s} s: check that the heater is connected and that the sensor is attached to it.

startup.state_na: does not apply to your machine
startup.make_tip: Copies the example to the SD card. It never overwrites a file that already exists.
startup.edit_tip: Opens the file in the DWC editor.

startup.service_tip: It has to be running: it makes the examples and answers the buttons of this plugin.
startup.assist_tip: Walks you through what is missing, one thing at a time. You can skip what you do not need.
startup.assist_no_action: This cannot be fixed with a file from here. Read the explanation and, when you have it, tap "Check again".
startup.assist_done_ready: Everything you went through is ready.
startup.assist_done_left: {n} left to do. You can start again whenever you like.
startup.create_help_tip: Asks a few questions and builds the file. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
startup.questions_intro: Answer and I will build the file. Nothing is saved until you confirm.

startup.err_chars: Do not use quotes, semicolons or line breaks.

fff.too_big: The file is too big to read here: the layers are spread evenly between the lowest and the highest Z.
fff.reading: Reading the layers of the file: {pct} %
fff.layers_differ: The file has {a} layers but the plan has {b}: the layers are spread evenly between the lowest and the highest Z.
fff.read_error: Could not read the file ({e}): the layers are spread evenly between the lowest and the highest Z.
fff.only_fff: The 3D view is only for 3D prints.
fff.no_job: Pick a file and press View in 3D.
fff.nothing: Nothing is printed in this file.
fff.no_files: There are no G-code files in 0:/gcodes.
fff.no_layers: This file has no extrusion (it looks like a laser or CNC file): there are no 3D printing layers to show. Pick a 3D printing file.

errors.need_technician: Saving {file} needs the technician or administrator role. Ask a technician for help.
errors.need_login: Identify yourself with your name and PIN to save {file}.

nozzle.title: Nozzle change
nozzle.intro: The firmware does not know the nozzle diameter: this guide takes you through the change (hot, because the pellet inside is hard when cold) and tells you what to redo with the new diameter.
nozzle.invalid_diameter: Enter a diameter between 0.2 and 8 mm.
nozzle.same_diameter: It is the same diameter as the registered one: you can still follow the steps (for example to clean or replace a worn nozzle).
nozzle.step_heat_detail: It only heats this tool; it does not move the machine.
nozzle.over_limit: It is above the zone limit ({c} °C).
nozzle.step_wait_hot: Wait until the nozzle reaches {c} °C or more
nozzle.hot_no_reading_check: I checked by hand that the pellet is soft (the sensor does not read)
nozzle.step_remove: Take the old nozzle off, hot
nozzle.step_remove_detail: With gloves and a wrench: it is above 150 °C. Let the molten pellet run out and clean the thread.
nozzle.removed: Old nozzle out and thread clean
nozzle.step_fit_detail: Tighten it hot so it does not leak when it cools, without over-torquing.
nozzle.saved_now_redo: {d} mm nozzle registered. This has to be redone with that diameter:
nozzle.follow_flow: The real flow per mm of E changes with the nozzle: calibrate by weight in “Extruder”.
nozzle.follow_stall: Going from {old} mm to {d} mm raises the back pressure and the screw torque. Lower the maximum speed and test the motor at low flow before printing, in case it stalls.
nozzle.follow_pid: The thermal mass of zone 1 changes: repeat the automatic PID.
nozzle.follow_pressure: The pressure lag of the molten pellet depends on the diameter: set it again with a test piece.
nozzle.follow_zoffset_title: Z height of the first layer
nozzle.follow_zoffset: The tip is in another position: check Z before printing.
nozzle.follow_slicer: Line width from {lineMin} to {lineMax} mm and layer height up to {layerMax} mm (80 % of the diameter). No retraction or a minimal one: pellet hardly needs it.
nozzle.profile_title: There is a saved profile for the {d} mm nozzle
nozzle.profile_found: Saved on {date}. Applying it puts back what was calibrated with that nozzle:
nozzle.profile_applied: Profile applied: {list}. It was sent to the machine and written to the configuration. Print a test piece to confirm.
nozzle.profile_none: There is no saved profile for {d} mm: what you calibrate now (flow, PID, pressure advance) is saved only for this nozzle.
nozzle.profile_kept: What was calibrated with the {d} mm nozzle was saved: if you fit it again, the profile applies with one tap.
nozzle.log_profile_applied: Profile of the {d} mm nozzle applied: {list}
nozzle.profiles_none: None yet: they are saved by themselves when you calibrate the flow, the PID and the pressure advance with a registered nozzle.
nozzle.first_intro: What the machine has today (flow, PID, pressure advance) was calibrated with the nozzle that is fitted. Tell me its diameter and I keep it as that nozzle's profile.
nozzle.first_done: {d} mm nozzle registered and its calibrations kept as its profile.
nozzle.log_first: {d} mm nozzle registered with the current calibrations

jobControl.title: Job control
jobControl.only_fff: The controls only work in FFF mode.
jobControl.help_what: What it is: the controls of the print in progress: pause, resume or cancel, and the live corrections the board accepts (Z height, speed and flow).
jobControl.help_why: What for: fix a first layer that does not stick or squashes, slow down or speed up without restarting, and stop the job in a controlled way.
jobControl.help_missing: Without it: the only way out is the main page of DWC or the emergency stop, which leaves neither the nozzle nor the part in order.
jobControl.help_how: How: with a job running tap Pause; once paused, Resume or Cancel (two taps); the Z steps and the percentages apply at once and last until the board restarts or the file changes them.
jobControl.job_help: Pause runs pause.g (it parks the nozzle and lowers the heaters when it is written so); Resume goes back to the point; Cancel (only while paused, like DWC) runs cancel.g and ends the job for good.
jobControl.live_job: A live job has its controls in the Jog bar.
jobControl.baby_help: What it is: it moves the nozzle a few hundredths without touching the file; negative brings it closer to the bed (the layer squashes more), positive lifts it. What for: the first layer, while watching the line. Without it: stop and fix the Z zero. How: one tap per step; the sum is lost when the board restarts and does not change the saved Z zero.
jobControl.baby_limit: Cap: +/-{limit} mm in total; more than that is a wrong Z zero, not a correction.
jobControl.speed_help: What it is: the speed (M220) as a percentage over the speeds of the file; 100 % is what the file asks. What for: slow a part that wobbles or speed up an infill. Without it: the file rules. How: type the percentage and Apply; lost when the board restarts.
jobControl.flow_help: What it is: the flow (M221, per extruder) as a percentage over the extrusion the file asks. What for: lower it when plastic is left over (rough edges) or raise it when lines are missing. Without it: the file rules. How: type the percentage and Apply; if you always need it, calibrate the flow in Extruder.

filament.only_fff: Loading material only works in FFF mode.
filament.help_what: What it is: a short assistant to feed filament into a tool or take it out: it heats to the temperature of the material, pushes or pulls a length at a safe speed and cools down at the end.
filament.help_why: What for: change material or colour without typing codes and without forcing the extruder with a cold nozzle.
filament.help_missing: Without it: loading is done by hand from the console (M701/M702 or G1 E) and it is easy to extrude cold or ask for more length than the tube takes.
filament.help_how: How: pick the material, Heat (two taps), wait for "ready", Load or Unload (two taps) and Cool down if you are not printing now. With the filament macros of the board (0:/filaments/(name)/load.g and unload.g) M701 and M702 are used; without them the extruder is moved with the length and the speed below. Nothing moves below the minimum extrusion temperature of the board.
filament.material_help: What it is: the material you are loading; its nozzle temperature comes from the Materials table. What for: heat just enough for the plastic to flow. Without it: "Temperature of the tool" uses the target the tool already has; without a target there is nothing to heat to. How: pick it and tap Heat.
filament.no_temp: No temperature: pick a material or set a target in Status.
filament.macro_help: What it is: the filament macros of the board (0:/filaments/{name}/load.g and unload.g); M701 runs load.g and M702 the unload.g of what is loaded. What for: follow the sequence the technician wrote. If one is missing: that button moves the extruder directly with the length and the speed below. How: two taps.
filament.direct_help: What it is: the length pushed (load) or pulled (unload) and the speed of the extruder. What for: go from the inlet of the extruder to the nozzle (direct: 60-120 mm; Bowden: the length of the tube) without grinding the filament. Without it: a short length and the plastic does not show; a high speed and the wheel slips. How: type them and tap Load or Unload.
filament.block_no_tool: No tool with a nozzle heater in FFF mode.
filament.block_job: A job is running: wait for it to end or pause it.
filament.block_fault: The nozzle reads no temperature or is in fault: fix it before moving the extruder.
filament.block_cold: The nozzle is below {min} °C (the minimum extrusion temperature of the board): heat first.
filament.bad_form: Check the length and the speed (out of limits).
filament.after_help: What it is: the wrap-up. What for: not leaving the nozzle hot for nothing (the plastic degrades and oozes). Without it: the heater stays on until someone turns it off. How: Cool down if you are not printing now; if the line comes out uneven, purge in Extruder (technician).
